vignette: A 30-year-old man is stabbed in the back at the level of the lower thoracic spine. He has weakness of the right leg with a brisk knee jerk and an upgoing toe, cannot feel a tuning fork on the right ankle, and cannot feel a pin on the left leg below the groin.
stem: Which pathway accounts for the left-sided finding?
explanation: Pain and temperature fibers cross in the anterior white commissure within a segment or two of entry, so the right spinothalamic tract carries pain from the left leg; a right hemicord lesion therefore gives left pain loss with right weakness and right proprioceptive loss (Brown-Séquard).
